name: Kingen
description: Kingen (also known as King) is a Belgian and French trick-taking game played by four individuals. It is a 'compendium' game where a full session consists of a series of rounds with different objectivesâ€”some rounds are 'negative' (avoiding specific tricks or cards) while others are 'positive' (trying to win tricks). It is the European parent of the game Barbu.

history.origins: Dates to the early 20th century in Western Europe. It evolved from simpler 'penalty' games like Hearts into a structured multi-round tournament format favored by university students and social clubs.
timeline: 1920s: King spreads in French-speaking card clubs.
1970s: The game is exported to the UK and USA as 'Barbu'.
Present: A very common social game in Flanders and Francophone Belgium.
Modern: Digital versions like 'Kingen.be' maintain a competitive player base.
history.cultural: In Belgium, it is a staple of 'cafÃ© culture' and social gatherings.
history.evolution: The game's variety (changing rules every round) makes it more dynamic than Bridge while retaining significant strategic depth.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Aces are high, 2s are low.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 13 cards. The role of dealer rotates clockwise.

rules.objective: Have the highest cumulative score after all rounds (Negative + Positive) are completed.
rules.gameplay:
1. Must follow suit. If unable, play any card (in negative rounds) or trump (in positive rounds).
2. Scoring varies by house; common penalty is -5 for hearts, -20 for queens, etc.
keyRules: Negative rounds: avoid winning specific tricks or cards
Positive rounds: try to win tricks
Each round has different scoring objectives
King of Hearts (Barbu) is the most critical card

strategy.basic: Keep track of the 'King of Hearts' (The Kingen). In the Kingen round, dumping this card on an opponent is the single most important tactical move.
strategy.intermediate: Strategic Leading: If you have a weak hand, lead suits where you have middle-rank cards (7, 8, 9) to force opponents to win tricks with their 10s and face cards.
strategy.advanced: Void Management: Purposely exhaust your shortest suit early. This allows you to 'slough' (discard) your penalty cards (Queens/Hearts) safely onto tricks won by others.
tips: In the 'Last Two' round, count your 2s and 3s. You must save them to ensure you don't 'climb' into the 12th or 13th trick.
Pay attention to the dealer; their choice of trump suit will tell you everything about their hand strength.
